instructions: Heat the oven to 360°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mash the 2 bananas with a fork until they're smooth with only small lumps left.
Add the 2 cups oats and stir with a spatula until it comes together into a thick, sticky dough.
Scoop the dough into 9 balls and set them on the sheet about 2 inches apart.
Press each ball flat into a cookie about 1/2 inch thick. They don't spread in the oven.
Press the 2 tbsp mini chocolate chips into the tops.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until they're set and the bottoms are lightly golden. This makes 9 cookies.
Leave them on the sheet for 5 minutes, then move them to a rack to cool.
Keep them in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 4 days.
method_notes: All three mash ripe banana, stir in oats, shape flat rounds that don't spread and bake them at about 350°F. Matt's Fit Chef (the lead) uses 2 large bananas to 2 cups rolled oats, bakes 9 cookies for 8 to 10 minutes at 360°F and tops them with chocolate chips. A Pretty Life in the Suburbs uses less oats and bakes longer, and Bob's Red Mill uses 1 banana to 1 cup quick oats and keeps them up to 4 days. This follows the lead and leaves out its optional maple syrup or honey.
